es: Reconocer metáforas cotidianas (feel down, a warm welcome, time is running out, a bright idea), entender su significado no literal y valorar qué actitud transmiten en correos, reuniones y opiniones.

vocabulary.es: literal, al pie de la letra

teaching.en: When we finally reached the village, the owner gave us such a warm welcome that the long, tiring journey was forgotten at once.
teaching.es: Cuando por fin llegamos al pueblo, el dueño nos dio una bienvenida tan cálida que el largo y cansado viaje se olvidó al instante.
teaching.explanationEs: A warm welcome es una metáfora: la bienvenida no tiene temperatura, pero transmite afecto y cercanía.
segments: When we finally reached the village, the owner gave us such a
warm welcome that the long, tiring journey was forgotten at once.
teaching.audioText: When we finally reached the village, the owner gave us such a warm welcome that the long, tiring journey was forgotten at once.

teaching.en: After weeks of bad news she began to feel down, and even the simplest decisions seemed heavy to her.
teaching.es: Tras semanas de malas noticias empezó a sentirse decaída, y hasta las decisiones más simples le parecían pesadas.
teaching.explanationEs: Feel down y heavy traducen la tristeza como dirección hacia abajo y como peso; no hay caída ni peso reales.
segments: After weeks of bad news she began to feel down,
and even the simplest decisions seemed heavy to her.
teaching.audioText: After weeks of bad news she began to feel down, and even the simplest decisions seemed heavy to her.

teaching.en: Time is running out, and a flood of unanswered requests is making the whole department nervous about Friday's deadline.
teaching.es: Se está acabando el tiempo, y una avalancha de peticiones sin responder pone nervioso a todo el departamento por el plazo del viernes.
teaching.explanationEs: Time is running out imagina el tiempo como algo que se vacía; a flood of + plural indica una cantidad abrumadora.
segments: Time is running out, and a flood of unanswered requests
is making the whole department nervous about Friday's deadline.
teaching.audioText: Time is running out, and a flood of unanswered requests is making the whole department nervous about Friday's deadline.

teaching.en: Calling an idea bright is ordinary imagery, because light stands for intelligence, which is why Ana's bright plan impressed everybody.
teaching.es: Llamar brillante a una idea es una imagen corriente, porque la luz representa la inteligencia, y por eso el plan brillante de Ana impresionó a todos.
teaching.explanationEs: Imagery es el conjunto de imágenes que usamos al hablar; bright idea asocia la luz con la claridad mental.
segments: Calling an idea bright is ordinary imagery, because light stands
for intelligence, which is why Ana's bright plan impressed everybody.
teaching.audioText: Calling an idea bright is ordinary imagery, because light stands for intelligence, which is why Ana's bright plan impressed everybody.

teaching.en: After a week in Lima, Tom said the city is a jungle because every driver, vendor and pedestrian competes for the same small space.
teaching.es: Después de una semana en Lima, Tom dijo que la ciudad es una selva porque cada conductor, vendedor y peatón compite por el mismo espacio pequeño.
teaching.explanationEs: The city is a jungle es una metáfora: no hay árboles ni animales, pero la imagen transmite caos y competencia.
segments: After a week in Lima, Tom said the city is a jungle
because every driver, vendor and pedestrian competes for the same small space.
teaching.audioText: After a week in Lima, Tom said the city is a jungle because every driver, vendor and pedestrian competes for the same small space.

teaching.en: A writer chooses a metaphor to convey a feeling quickly, whereas a literal description would need several careful sentences to do the same.
teaching.es: Un escritor elige una metáfora para transmitir un sentimiento con rapidez, mientras que una descripción literal necesitaría varias frases cuidadosas para lo mismo.
teaching.explanationEs: Metaphor es lo figurado; literal es lo que significa exactamente lo que dicen las palabras.
segments: A writer chooses a metaphor to convey a feeling quickly, whereas a
literal description would need several careful sentences to do the same.
teaching.audioText: A writer chooses a metaphor to convey a feeling quickly, whereas a literal description would need several careful sentences to do the same.

prompt.es: ¿Qué sentido tienen «feel down» y «heavy heart» en el mensaje de Leo?

choices.text: He is sad and disappointed, so he asks for more time.
He is ill and tired, so he will stay in bed today.
He is angry about the budget, so he wants to leave.

feedback.es: Las dos expresiones hablan del ánimo, no del cuerpo: Leo está desanimado por el presupuesto y por eso pide aplazar el informe.

hint.es: Ninguna de las dos expresiones habla de peso físico ni de una caída: fíjate en el estado de ánimo.

origin.text: Leo wrote to his manager: 'I feel down today. The news about the budget has left me with a heavy heart, and I would like to finish the report tomorrow instead of tonight.'

prompt.es: Completa: «En cuanto salió la noticia, una avalancha de llamadas llegó a la oficina.»

feedback.es: A flood of + plural expresa una cantidad enorme que llega de golpe, como una inundación de llamadas.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo de agua que usamos para decir «muchísimas cosas a la vez».

origin.text: The moment the news was published, a ___ of calls hit the office. Nobody had expected so many, and the phones never stopped ringing.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Su cálida bienvenida transmitió más que cualquier discurso.»

answer.text: Her warm welcome conveyed more than any speech

feedback.es: El sujeto es her warm welcome y conveyed lleva el significado de la metáfora: el afecto dice más que las palabras.

hint.es: Empieza con Her warm welcome y termina con la palabra speech.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué ayudó a la hermana de la narradora.

choices.text: A long phone call with her family at home.
The friendly way her neighbours received her.
The calm and sunny weather in her new town.

feedback.es: «A warm welcome» se refiere a la acogida de los vecinos: eso cambió su ánimo; la llamada y el tiempo no se citan como ayuda.

origin.audio: I called my sister last night. She has just moved abroad, and she sounded a little down. She told me she felt like a small boat in a big storm, and that her heart was heavy whenever she thought of home. Then her voice changed, because the neighbours had given her a warm welcome, and that made her first week easier.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase metafórica con su traducción natural.

pairs: Our neighbours gave us a warm welcome.

pairs.es: Nuestros vecinos nos acogieron con cariño.

pairs: The schedule is a jungle of meetings.

pairs.es: El horario es un caos enmarañado de reuniones.

pairs: A flood of orders arrived in December.

pairs.es: Llegó una avalancha de pedidos en diciembre.

pairs: He had a bright idea about the budget.

pairs.es: Tuvo una idea inteligente sobre el presupuesto.

feedback.es: Cada metáfora se traduce por su efecto: acogida afectuosa, caos, cantidad abrumadora e inteligencia.

prompt.es: Lee las tres frases del blog: ¿en cuál se usa «warm» en sentido literal?

choices.text: The welcome that the village gave the travellers.
The market, full of sellers and bicycles everywhere.
The warm room, heated all night.

feedback.es: Solo la habitación tiene una temperatura real gracias a la calefacción; la bienvenida y el mercado son imágenes.

origin.text: Travel blog: 'The village gave us a warm welcome. Our room was warm because the heating was on all night. The market, however, was a jungle of shouting sellers and bicycles.'

prompt.es: Escucha la reunión y elige qué espera la directora de su equipo.

choices.text: Proposals that solve problems, not more complaints.
Detailed reports on every request she has received.
Silence from everybody until the board has decided.

feedback.es: Pide que cada problema llegue con «a bright idea»: espera soluciones, no más quejas; no pide informes ni silencio.

origin.audio: At Monday's meeting, our manager opened with a long silence. She said the department had become a jungle this month: every team was fighting for the same budget, and a flood of requests had landed on her desk. She added that time was running out before the board meets, and that she did not want to hear about another problem unless it came with a bright idea. Then she smiled and thanked us for our patience.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué actitud deja entender el tono de la directora.

choices.text: She is angry and holds the whole team responsible for it.
She is under pressure, but she still appreciates the team.
She is relaxed and believes the deadline can move.

feedback.es: El silencio inicial y las imágenes muestran presión, pero termina sonriendo y agradeciendo la paciencia: valora al equipo.

origin.audio: At Monday's meeting, our manager opened with a long silence. She said the department had become a jungle this month: every team was fighting for the same budget, and a flood of requests had landed on her desk. She added that time was running out before the board meets, and that she did not want to hear about another problem unless it came with a bright idea. Then she smiled and thanked us for our patience.

prompt.es: Completa: «Al oír la decisión, salió con el corazón encogido sin decir nada.»

feedback.es: A heavy heart es la colocación fija para la tristeza que pesa: no se dice «a weight heart» ni «a big heart».

origin.text: When she heard the decision, she said nothing. She simply picked up her bag and left the room with a ___ heart, and her colleagues understood how disappointed she was.

prompt.es: ¿Qué postura defiende la autora sobre las metáforas cotidianas?

choices.text: They are popular, but they make writing less clear.
They should be avoided in careful professional writing.
They are useful tools for expressing feeling quickly.

feedback.es: La autora contradice a los críticos: en dos palabras la metáfora comunica lo que una descripción literal tardaría un párrafo en decir.

origin.text: Critics often say that everyday metaphors are lazy. I disagree. When a colleague tells me she feels down, she conveys in two words what a literal description of her mood would need a whole paragraph to explain, and everybody understands her at once.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito escribe la directora este correo a los equipos?

choices.text: To encourage the teams and collect ideas without adding pressure.
To warn the teams that they must work late until Friday.
To announce that the teams will receive fewer requests.

feedback.es: Reconoce el cansancio, descarta las horas extra y solo pide una idea pequeña: busca motivar y reunir propuestas sin presionar.

origin.text: Dear all, I know the last weeks have been a jungle, and a flood of requests has left many of you feeling down. I am not asking anyone to work late. I simply want each team to send me one bright idea by Friday, however small, so that we can decide before time runs out.

prompt.es: Completa: «El estudio era una selva durante la última semana del proyecto.»

feedback.es: Jungle es la metáfora del caos y del ruido donde cada uno lucha por hacerse oír, no una descripción de plantas.

origin.text: Everyone agreed that the studio was a ___ during the last week of the project: phones rang all day, people shouted across the room, and nobody could hear anybody else.

prompt.es: Escucha el discurso de despedida y elige qué deja entender la directora de Tom.

choices.text: That the project will continue without any change at all.
That his departure will be a real loss for the team.
That she is relieved because he is finally leaving.

feedback.es: Llamarlo «the heart of the team» y decir que la oficina se sentirá fría sin él implica que su marcha será una pérdida real.

origin.audio: When Tom left the company, his manager called him the heart of the team. She said the office would feel cold without him, and that his bright ideas had kept the project alive for years. Tom smiled, but he admitted that he felt heavy as he packed his things.
